root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `ndpi_handle_rule()` aliases `def` to `ndpi_str->proto_defaults[proto_id]`, the selected `proto_id` must remain strictly within the allocated `proto_defaults` table.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable run returns from `ndpi_set_proto_defaults()` after `ndpi_realloc()` fails, leaving `ndpi_str->proto_defaults_num_allocated` unchanged at the old bound while `proto_id` still names the first free slot. The fixed code restores the missing obligation by checking the growth result before allowing the alias and later `tcp:` walk.

nodes.state: The growth attempt returns `NULL`, so `ndpi_set_proto_defaults()` exits without updating either `ndpi_str->proto_defaults` or `ndpi_str->proto_defaults_num_allocated`.
After the failed growth, `def = &ndpi_str->proto_defaults[proto_id]` forms a pointer strictly past the last valid allocated slot in the unchanged `proto_defaults` array.
The `tcp:` port loop dereferences the same `def` pointer that was formed by the out-of-bounds alias, so the sink read executes on stale out-of-bounds state.

edges.relation: The first-free custom-protocol slot chosen from `ndpi_str->num_supported_protocols` is the same `proto_id` later checked against the unchanged allocation bound at the root guard.
Because `ndpi_realloc()` failed, the old `ndpi_str->proto_defaults_num_allocated` value carries unchanged from the failure return back to the root alias site.
The out-of-bounds `def` alias formed after the failed growth is forwarded unchanged into the later `tcp:` default-port loop and becomes the pointer dereferenced at the sanitizer sink.
